notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — three P0 issues are workspace-pre-push-check failures (clippy --tests, cargo doc --all-features); none would change shipped behaviour, but all three would block AGENTS.md's published pre-push gate. Plus a documented contradiction between the # Limitations rustdoc and the 0.3.1 CHANGELOG about whether tc60 is resolved. None of the P0/P1 findings indicate a wrong-on-the-spec bug. The trait surface and Error shape are forward-compatible (#[non_exhaustive]). Risk is doc-fidelity and CI-discipline, not behavioural correctness.
Confidence: 5% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: PKIX-wnnn.7 (pkix-chain NoValidPath as non-recoverable) — the adversarial cross-cert AIA scenario I describe is constructible but I have not built one to confirm; the finding is a doc/operational gap, not a correctness claim against demonstrated input. Uncertainty driven by: no probe was run against an actual cross-signed federal-bridge fixture (skipped per /review-myoss read-only rule); the 25 bettertls fixtures committed in this diff don't exercise that case. Would raise confidence if: a fixture from a real federal-bridge cross-cert pool was added, or a unit test in pkix-chain explicitly exercises the NoValidPath then AIA fetches the right cross-cert path.
API contract risk: LOW — eight api-contract findings filed (PKIX-wnnn.19 through .26). The one P1 (struct-variant exhaustiveness on Error::NoValidPath) is a permanent shape commitment that becomes locked-in once 1.0 ships, but is a one-attribute fix today; the P2s are doc-only (serde format stability, last_error format stability, time-complexity contract); the P3s are minor doc inaccuracies. No findings under api-contract,versioning / leakage / defensive — that ground was either covered by the prior review (PKIX-wnnn.5 closes off the leakage angle on String) or genuinely empty in this diff. The new public surface (build_first_valid_path, Error::NoValidPath, serde feature on Error) is acceptable to depend on as-is provided the P1 is addressed before 1.0.
API contract confidence: 10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: (a) PKIX-wnnn.20 (serde wire format) — I reasoned from serde's default external-tag behaviour without comparing pkix-path's existing serde-on-Error practice; if pkix-path already documents the same trade-off elsewhere in the workspace and pkix-path-builder consciously mirrors it, my finding is partially redundant; (b) PKIX-wnnn.19 (struct-variant exhaustiveness) is sound on the Rust language spec but I did not run cargo-semver-checks against a hypothetical "add field to NoValidPath" delta to confirm it flags as breaking. Uncertainty driven by: (1) no probe of cargo-semver-checks output, (2) no cross-read of pkix-path / pkix-revocation / pkix-chain Error types to see if the workspace has an established pattern for struct-variant evolution that this diff implicitly conforms to, (3) cargo doc was not run, so the intra-doc link rendering in PKIX-wnnn.24 is inferred from rustdoc reference-syntax rules rather than observed in the generated HTML. Would raise confidence if: (a) cargo-semver-checks output on a synthetic future-state branch confirms PKIX-wnnn.19's breaking-change classification, (b) a brief sibling-crate read confirms whether pkix-path's serde Error pattern matches or differs.
